subject: POC: workload profile & success metrics — next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finex.io>, Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff — workload profile & success criteria (recap)

Hi Elena / Martin —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before I put the SOW on DocuSign. Key points from today’s discovery and the items we need from your side to scope the trial: 

1) High-level POC goals (you confirmed):
- Validate latency and throughput for the anomaly-detection inference path (text->scored output).
- Verify model quality on the 500-sample eval set (pass rate >= 85% per your internal rubric).
- Measure cost per 1k tokens and p95 latency under representative load.

2) Workload / traffic intake (please confirm values below; if we got anything wrong, correct inline):
- Steady-state RPS: ~8 req/s
- Peak bursts: up to ~80 req/s for 20–40s at a time (spikes associated with batch re-scoring jobs)
- Prompt (input) length: median ~120 tokens, 95th pct ~420 tokens
- Response (output) length: median ~300 tokens, 95th pct ~900 tokens
- Concurrency: ~10 concurrent sessions (mostly API single-call workflows)
- Auth & security: TLS + customer allowlist will be required; SOC2 evidence requested during onboarding

3) Success criteria we discussed:
- Performance: p95 latency < 250 ms for single-turn inference at steady-state, and graceful degradation with fallback during bursts
- Quality: >=85% pass rate on your eval set (we’ll agree on scoring CSV)
- Cost: provide a target cost-per-1k tokens we should aim to stay under during the 10-day eval window

4) Deliverables we’ll provide:
- SOW & trial quota (attached): redwood-poc-sow.pdf
- Instrumented endpoints for test traffic and a short runbook for our SDK
- Trial dashboard access + short checklist for telemetry to collect

Next steps / asks from Finex:
- Confirm the workload numbers above (RPS, token lengths, burst profile) — if possible send 48–72 hours of sample traffic in CSV format. Fields we’ll need: timestamp, request_id, prompt_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, user_id (can be hashed), response_time_ms.
- Confirm customer POC lead (who will own sign-off on the success criteria)
- If the timeline looks good, we propose kickoff next Wednesday (2026-03-25) and data handoff by Tue 2026-03-24.

I’ve attached the SOW draft for review. Ben (SE) and Marissa (CS) are looped in to scope the runbook and metrics collection.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the DocuSign link once you confirm.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood-poc-sow.pdf
From: Elena Rossi <elena@finex.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — workload profile & success criteria (recap)

Thanks Rafael — good summary. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

- The steady-state number is correct (8 RPS). The big bursts happen when our batch re-score job kicks off — those typically reach ~80 RPS for short intervals (20–40s), occasionally up to 120 RPS but only for <15s.
- Prompt lengths: median 110–130 tokens, 95th 400–800 depending on user segment; responses average 250–350 tokens.
- Concurrency: we have ~10 long-lived sessions but higher short-term concurrency (up to ~25) during peak business hours.

POC lead: Martin Kline (cc’d) will be the internal owner and sign-off. He will share a sanitized traffic sample (we will redact PII) — Martin, can you confirm you can deliver the CSV by Tue end-of-day PST?

Success criteria: Confirmed on our side — particularly the quality metric is the most important. We’ll provide the 500-sample eval and the scoring rubric before the kickoff.

One question: for the latency target, can Redwood confirm whether p95 < 250ms is for token-to-token generation or end-to-end request completion? We’re thinking end-to-end (i.e., from request arrival to final response).

Elena
Head of Product
Finex Analytics
elena@finex.io

On Fri, Mar 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see above)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finex.io>, Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — workload profile & success criteria (recap)

Thanks Elena — good catches. To confirm on the latency wording: when we say p95 < 250 ms we mean end-to-end request completion from API ingress to final payload delivered. That includes network + inference time for the single-turn path. During bursts we expect p95 to increase; our goal is graceful degradation and an agreed fallback (e.g., shorter responses or model variant) rather than hard failures.

Action items I’ll take on now: 
- Publish SOW to DocuSign by EOD (attached SOW still in draft; will send link).
- Template for traffic CSV with column names and a short sample — Martin, sending the CSV template will make the handoff faster.

Martin — can you confirm who on your team will be the data contact (email) and whether the sample can be scrubbed of PII? If you prefer, we can accept a sampled/aggregated extract that preserves timing and token distributions.

Ben / Marissa — looping you to draft the trial runbook and to propose exact telemetry we’ll surface in the dashboard (p95, p99, token counts, cost per 1k tokens, error rates).

Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@finex.io>, Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood POC runbook & timeline

Hi all —

Quick draft plan from CS/solutions to make the POC execution frictionless. Rafael, feel free to forward to Finex.

POC roles (confirmed):
- Redwood POC owner (sales): Rafael Mendes
- Redwood Solutions Eng: Ben Carter
- Finex POC owner (customer): Martin Kline

Timeline (target):
- Tue 2026-03-24: Data + traffic sample delivered to secure bucket (customer to provide)
- Wed 2026-03-25: Kickoff call (15–30m) — onboarding + runbook review
- Thu–Sat 2026-03-26 to 2026-03-28: Baseline run (sanity checks, smoke tests)
- Sun–Sat 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-07: Evaluation window (10 days)
- Mon 2026-04-08: Final sync and sign-off (pass/fail + next steps)

Success metrics (proposed):
- Performance: p95 end-to-end latency < 250ms at steady-state; p95 < 450ms during bursts with graceful fallbacks
- Quality: >=85% pass rate on your 500-sample eval set (we will accept the Finex scoring CSV)
- Stability: error rate < 0.5% during the evaluation window

Telemetry we will surface in the dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens in/out, requests per second, cost per 1k tokens (running), error codes, sample outputs for manual review. We’ll provide a short SDK instrumentation checklist to include headers that allow us to correlate requests (request_id, session_id).

Data/traffic format: please provide a CSV with columns: timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, prompt_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, response_time_ms, user_hash. If you cannot provide user_hash, a uniformly hashed id or sampling rate is fine. Please redact PII before uploading.

Security / onboarding: We’ll need a list of inbound IPs if you prefer allowlisting, and your SOC2 questionnaire responses (we can accept a copy of your vendor risk form if needed).

Attachments: redwood-poc-runbook.docx (I’ll put the link in the Drive folder)

If the above looks good, Rafael — we’ll schedule Ben for the kickoff and I’ll provision dashboard access ahead of the baseline run.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 22:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood POC runbook & timeline — sample delivery confirmed

Rafael / Marissa — thanks, plan looks good.

I’ll own the sample delivery. We’ll produce a 72-hour traffic extract and scrub PII — expected CSV to include: timestamp, request_id, prompt_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, response_time_ms, user_id_hashed. We’ll also include a small eval CSV (500 rows) and the scoring rubric.

We can deliver the files by Tue EOD PST (2026-03-24). Also: a quick question about connectivity — do you prefer we do IP allowlisting on our side or provide API keys over a VPN peering? We can do either; what’s easiest for Redwood?

Martin
Lead Data Engineer | Finex Analytics
mkline@finex.io
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Kline <mkline@finex.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood POC runbook & timeline — sample delivery confirmed

Martin — perfect, thanks. IP allowlisting is easiest for a quick POC (we’ll send our ingress IPs and CSR for TLS); if you want to explore VPN/peering for Dedicated later we can scope that separately.

I’ll send the DocuSign link after midday and Ben will join the kickoff. Looking forward to the 03/25 call.

— Rafael
